data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption is permitted if and only if the event framing protocol deterministically identifies trailing bytes from budget exhaustion as an incomplete, uncommitted fragment (a non-event), and is refused if such trailing bytes are indistinguishable from a corrupted complete event.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The framing protocol uses length-prefixing alone without end-markers, making a partial event indistinguishable from a complete one and corrupting causal continuity upon resumption.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Budget exhaustion occurs between an event's data write and a subsequent mandatory commit record, leaving a structurally complete but logically uncommitted event that naive framing would incorrectly validate.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The resumption protocol attempts to overwrite or garbage-collect the trailing partial bytes in place, violating the physical append-only integrity of the log.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Self-delimiting framing with checksums causes the resumption protocol to recognize trailing bytes lacking a valid end-marker as non-events. Since non-events lack event identity, they were never committed to the logical stream. This causal separation means ignoring them does not delete or modify a committed event, preserving physical append-only integrity (SCR_006), while causal continuity (SCR_007) is preserved by resuming from the last validly framed event.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
